messages:
maya: Noticed during the usability session: new users get stuck on the credentials page empty state. They try to click the main CTA but arent sure which key type to create or which permissions to pick.

kai: Yep. We surfaced about 6 support tickets last week that are "I rotated my key and now my webhook is broken" or "Which key do I give to the analytics service?".

olivia: The empty state copy is short but feels vague. Current CTA is just 'Create API key' 1 think we need a microflow that clarifies purpose.

maya: Proposal: split CTA into primary 'Create key (server)' and secondary 'Create key (client)'. Hover/help text explains default scopes and common use cases. Add a tiny decision tree: "server = long-lived, all scopes; client = limited, no admin scopes".

jenna: +1. Also add a small "use-case template" dropdown in the modal: e.g., Webhook consumer, Internal service, Front-end embed. Selecting one pre-checks recommended scopes and adds a 1-line why.

raghu: Accessibility nits: when opening the creation modal the first interactive control should be the key name field. Also validate scope checkboxes with aria-invalid if required. Screen reader users reported not catching the template dropdown because it's after a lot of helper text.

olivia: For copy we can do: primary line: "Create an API key to authenticate services". Below, helper: "Choose from presets for common use cases or customize scopes." Keep the helper short.

maya: UX tiny: show a summary panel on the right of the modal that updates as you change scopes/presets: short bullet list of permissions and an estimated blast radius label: Low / Medium / High. Each level has sr-only text like "High impact: could revoke access to production".

kai: Product ask: can that blast radius map to telemetry flags so we can detect risky keys? Would help for targeted onboarding nudges and reducing support.

jenna: Backend note: we can annotate keys with metadata risk_level during creation. We just need the UI to pass a field risk_level.

raghu: Ensure we don't rely on color to convey Low/Medium/High. Use icons and textual labels with sufficient contrast. Also ensure the summary panel is announced when it updates (aria-live="polite").

maya: Another empty-state thought: include a "Try with sample key" flow for new orgs that spins up a sandbox key and a short guided tutorial that posts a test call to the playground. That might cut the friction to ship.

olivia: Nice. The interactive tutorial could be one-click: "Create test key & run sample request". Show curl + JS snippets and an inline response preview.

kai: We should gate the sample key to not include admin scopes. It should be read-only or limited to the playground domain.

jenna: Agreed. We'll create a restricted template 'Playground' that can't be elevated. Implementation: backend creates token with scope set to ["read:models","playground:use"] and tag as sandbox.

raghu: Keyboard flow: when user clicks "Create test key & run sample request" keyboard focus should move to the response preview and user should be able to re-run with Enter. Also ensure the preview supports high-contrast mode.

maya: Microcopy suggestion for templates list: 'Webhook consumer — short-lived, no admin; Internal service — long-lived, can include read/write; Front-end embed — restricted, CORS-limited'. Keep it to single-line labels.

olivia: Figma WIP: https://www.figma.com/file/XXXXX/credentials-onboarding-redesign (WIP). I'll add variants for the modal and the sandbox flow.

kai: One more product constraint: we need to make sure rotate flow is discoverable from the key details page. Users in tests tried to find rotate in the three-dot menu but it was hidden under "more actions".

maya: Suggestion: always surface Rotate as a visible action if risk_level == High or the key is used by >1 live route. Otherwise keep it in overflow.

jenna: Backend can return usage_count; UI can add a badge when usage_count > 1.

raghu: Accessibility check for rotate: rotate modal should describe what rotation does (rotate secret, keep metadata, break existing tokens until swapped), and include a required checkbox "I understand rotating will break current consumers" with aria-required.

maya: Action items: olivia to update Figma prototypes (templates + sandbox flow), raghu to draft A11y checklist for the creation + rotate modals, jenna to confirm backend metadata fields (risk_level, usage_count, sandbox flag), kai to scope telemetry for risky-key events. I'll follow up to collate copy for the templates.

olivia: Will post prototypes and alt text examples here by EOD.

maya: Thanks all :sparkles: — goal is to reduce first-week support tickets by surfacing intent and safer defaults.

(End thread)
